_note: NB303: weakening phrases, grouped by what the fix actually is. 'cut' hedges come out and the claim survives intact. 'replace' hedges leave a shorter form behind. 'rewrite' hedges cannot be cut mechanically at all — the negated ones ('I don't think we should ship') invert the claim if you simply delete them, and the tentative ones state an intention the writer has to commit to. The rule decides replace-vs-rewrite for the first two groups by position: a hedge that opens a sentence or sits against a comma needs capitalization and punctuation cleanup, so it drops to rewrite.

rewrite.i don't believe: move the negation into the claim: 'X will not happen'
rewrite.i don't consider: move the negation into the claim: 'X is not Y'
rewrite.i don't feel: move the negation into the claim: 'X is not Y'
rewrite.i don't suggest: state the negative directly: 'do not do X'
rewrite.i don't think: move the negation into the claim: 'X will not work'
rewrite.i might: commit ('I will …') or cut the sentence
rewrite.we don't believe: move the negation into the claim: 'X will not happen'

rewrite.we don't feel: move the negation into the claim: 'X is not Y'
rewrite.we don't suggest: state the negative directly: 'do not do X'
rewrite.we don't think: move the negation into the claim: 'X will not work'
rewrite.we might: commit ('we will …') or cut the sentence
